subject: history
title: Life under the Nazis and the Holocaust
welcome_lead: Today you'll stretch — daily life, terror, propaganda and the Holocaust.
meta_desc: GCSE History stretch — Nazi society, women, youth, persecution and the Holocaust.
final_note: You can now describe life under Nazi rule and explain the road to the Holocaust.

walkthroughs.body_html:
The Nazis controlled minds and movement.

Joseph Goebbels ran propaganda — rallies, radio, film and posters. The Gestapo and SS terrorised opposition. Concentration camps held political prisoners from 1933.

Women were pushed out of jobs and politics. The slogan 'Kinder, Kuche, Kirche' told them to raise children for the Reich.

Boys joined the Hitler Youth, girls the League of German Maidens. Schools taught racial science and loyalty to Hitler.

The Nuremberg Laws of 1935 stripped Jews of citizenship. Kristallnacht in November 1938 destroyed Jewish shops and synagogues.

From 1941 the Nazis carried out the Holocaust — death camps like Auschwitz murdered around six million Jews, plus millions of Roma, Slavs, disabled people and political prisoners.

Ended hyperinflation
Started Hitler Youth
Heinrich Himmler
Hermann Goring
Joseph Goebbels
Reinhard Heydrich

mcqs.q: How did Hitler come to power in 1933?
options: Hitler seized power through a violent coup or revolution.
He was legally appointed Chancellor by President Hindenburg as part of a conservative political deal, after the Nazis became the largest party in the Reichstag.
Hitler won an outright majority in the 1932 presidential election.
The Nuremberg Laws were the post-war trial of Nazi leaders.

mcqs.q: When did the systematic mass murder of Jews begin?
options: The killings only began after Germany lost the Battle of Stalingrad.
Hitler won an outright majority in the 1932 presidential election.
Mass shootings by Einsatzgruppen began with Operation Barbarossa in June 1941; industrial extermination camps followed from 1942.
The Holocaust began as soon as Hitler came to power in 1933.
